headline: Models recover cell-state transitions from snapshot single-cell and spatial profiles
label: Single Cell Dynamics Modeling
summary: Snapshot single-cell and spatial data now support dynamics inference without repeated measurements of the same cell.
synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is inferring temporal dynamics from data that never observe the same cell twice, including static scRNA-seq snapshots and spatial transcriptomics. Methods impose structure through different routes. DynNet applies a biophysical Neural ODE to infer stochastic gene regulatory dynamics and cell fate landscapes from scRNA-seq snapshots. A cross-cohort optimal transport framework combined with RNA velocity maps macrophage state transitions across seven human atherosclerotic plaque cohorts. A contrastive learning model links scRNA-seq datasets to Perturb-seq to separate conserved from context-specific perturbation responses. TMEformer performs in silico perturbation of tumor programs from spatial transcriptomics, and TRINUS decouples lineage identity from niche pressure. Echo detects desynchronized gene expression and chromatin accessibility during cell-state transitions. What is new is explicit encoding of biophysical, geometric, or niche constraints into dynamic and perturbation models.
